q: The provisions relating to the Official Language of the Union are contained in the Constitution in:
e: Part XVII (Articles 343 to 351) is the Official Language part of the Constitution, dealing with the language of the Union, the States, the judiciary and special directives.

q: Article 351 of the Constitution deals with:

options.B: Directive for the development of the Hindi language
options.D: Constitution of the Official Language Commission

e: Article 351 lays down the duty of the Union to promote the spread of Hindi and to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all elements of India's composite culture.

q: Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that certain documents, such as resolutions, general orders, notifications, contracts and tender forms, shall be issued:
e: Section 3(3) lists documents such as resolutions, general orders, notifications, contracts and tender forms which must mandatorily be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Tamil Nadu falls in:
e: Tamil Nadu, a non-Hindi State, falls in Region C under the Official Language Rules, where Hindi targets are the lowest and English predominates.

q: The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language consists of:
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

q: Article 343 of the Constitution declares the Official Language of the Union to be:

options.D: Hindustani in Devanagari and Persian scripts

e: Article 343(1) declares Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union.

q: Under Article 343, the numerals to be used for official purposes of the Union are:

options.B: The international form of Indian numerals

e: Article 343 prescribes the international form of Indian numerals, and not Devanagari numerals, for the official purposes of the Union.

q: Article 343 originally provided for the continued use of English for official purposes of the Union for a period of:
e: Article 343 originally allowed English to continue for official purposes of the Union for fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, that is, up to 1965.

q: Article 344 of the Constitution provides for:

options.A: The Official Language of the States
options.B: The constitution of an Official Language Commission and a Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.C: Language of the Supreme Court and High Courts

e: Article 344 provides for the constitution of an Official Language Commission by the President and a Committee of Parliament to examine the Commission's recommendations.

q: Article 345 empowers:

options.A: Parliament to fix the official language of the Union
options.B: The State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of that State
options.C: The President to declare English as the link language
options.D: The Supreme Court to decide language disputes

e: Article 345 empowers the Legislature of a State to adopt by law one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as the official language of that State.

q: Article 348 lays down that the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts shall, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, be:

options.B: The language of the State concerned

e: Article 348 provides that the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts shall be English until Parliament by law otherwise provides.

q: Article 350B of the Constitution provides for:

options.A: A Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President
options.B: Grants for the promotion of Hindi
options.D: Instruction through the mother tongue at the primary stage

e: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to safeguards for linguistic minorities.

q: Hindi Diwas is celebrated on 14th September because:

options.A: The Official Languages Act was passed on that day
options.B: On 14th September 1949, the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as the Official Language (the Munshi-Ayyangar formula)
options.C: The first Official Language Commission was appointed on that day
options.D: The Official Language Rules were notified on that day

e: On 14 September 1949 the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as the Official Language under the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, and the day is therefore celebrated as Hindi Diwas.

q: Under the Official Languages Act/Rules, a letter received in Hindi by a Central Government office must be replied to:

options.D: In either Hindi or English, at the discretion of the dealing clerk

e: Under the Official Language Rules, a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent.

q: The responsibility for ensuring that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are issued in both Hindi and English rests with:

options.C: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.D: The Head of the Office alone

e: The responsibility for ensuring that documents specified in Section 3(3) are issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document.

q: The Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules were framed in the year:
e: The Official Languages (Use for Official Purposes of the Union) Rules were framed in 1976 under the Official Languages Act, 1963.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is placed in:
e: The Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands is placed in Region A for the purposes of the Official Language Rules.

q: Under the Annual Programme for progressive use of Hindi, the target for Hindi correspondence (letters originating in Hindi) from Region 'C' offices is:
e: The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' is now 60%. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Programme 2025-26, target table Item 1; effective 01.04.2025.)

q: Under the Annual Programme, the target fixed for noting on files in Hindi is:
e: The Annual Programme target for noting on files in Hindi is now 35%. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, Annual Programme 2025-26, target table Item 3; effective 01.04.2025.)

q: The Annual Programme for the implementation of the Official Language Policy of the Union is prepared by:

options.B: The Ministry of Home Affairs (Department of Official Language)

e: The Annual Programme for implementation of the Official Language Policy is prepared by the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs.

q: The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was constituted in the year:
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in 1976 under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.

q: The first Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language was:
e: Om Mehta was the first Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language constituted in 1976.

q: The first Official Language Commission, appointed in 1955, was headed by:
e: The first Official Language Commission, appointed in 1955, was headed by B. G. Kher and is therefore known as the Kher Commission.

q: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme for Central Government employees, the first prescribed course is:
e: Prabodh is the first and elementary course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme, prescribed for employees who are beginners in Hindi.

q: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff is:
e: Pragya is the final prescribed course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme for clerical (ministerial) staff, standing above Prabodh and Praveen.

q: A railway/Central Government employee who passes the Pragya examination with 70% or more marks is entitled to a cash award of:
e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: A Central Government employee is deemed to have acquired 'working knowledge' of Hindi if he has:

options.A: Merely studied in a Hindi-medium school
options.C: Worked in Region 'A' for five years
options.D: Been posted in the Rajbhasha section for one year

e: Passing the Pragya examination is the prescribed test by which an employee is deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.

q: At railway stations and offices, name boards, designation boards and sign boards are required to be displayed in three languages, in the order:
e: Name boards, designation boards and sign boards at stations are displayed in three languages in the order regional language, Hindi and English.

q: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in:
e: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in Official Language Policy implementation in Regions A and B.

q: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy in:
e: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield is awarded to the best (Adarsh) Division for excellence in Official Language Policy implementation in Region C.

q: Under Article 346 of the Constitution, the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another, shall be:

options.B: The language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes
options.C: The regional language of the State which receives the communication
options.D: The language spoken by the majority in the country

e: Article 346 provides that the language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for official purposes shall be the official language for communication between the Union and a State, or between one State and another.

q: Article 347 of the Constitution empowers the President to direct that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall also be officially recognised for specified purposes, if he is satisfied that:

options.A: A substantial proportion of the population of the State desires the use of that language to be recognised
options.B: The Governor of the State requests it in writing
options.C: The State Assembly passes a resolution by two-thirds majority
options.D: The Official Language Commission recommends it unanimously

e: Under Article 347, if a substantial proportion of the population of a State desires the use of a language spoken by them to be recognised, the President may direct its official recognition for specified purposes.

q: Under Article 350 of the Constitution, every person is entitled to submit a representation for the redress of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in:

options.C: Any of the languages used in the Union or in the State, as the case may be
options.D: Only the official language of the State concerned

e: Article 350 entitles every person to submit a representation for redress of grievances to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or the State.

q: Article 350A of the Constitution relates to:

options.A: The language of the Union Territories
options.B: The authoritative text of laws in Hindi
options.C: The language to be used in the Supreme Court
options.D: Facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups

e: Article 350A directs every State to endeavour to provide facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

q: Under Article 120 of the Constitution, business in Parliament shall be transacted in:

options.D: Any language included in the Eighth Schedule

e: Article 120 provides that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English.

q: Under Article 210 of the Constitution, business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in:

options.A: The official language of the Union only
options.C: The official language or languages of the State, or Hindi, or English

e: Article 210 provides that business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in the official language or languages of the State, or Hindi, or English.

q: Under Article 349 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, no Bill or amendment relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts could be introduced in either House of Parliament without:

options.A: The approval of the Prime Minister
options.B: The previous sanction of the President
options.C: The consent of the Chief Justice of India
options.D: A two-thirds majority of both Houses

e: Article 349 barred the introduction, during the first fifteen years of the Constitution, of any Bill or amendment relating to the language of the Supreme Court and High Courts without the previous sanction of the President.

q: Under Article 344(1) of the Constitution, the President shall constitute an Official Language Commission:

options.C: At the expiration of ten years from the commencement of the Constitution only
options.D: At the expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement

e: Article 344(1) requires the President to constitute an Official Language Commission at the expiration of five years from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of ten years from such commencement.

q: The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 consists of a Chairman and other members representing:

options.A: The different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule
options.C: Only scholars of Hindi and Sanskrit

e: The Official Language Commission under Article 344 consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule.

q: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language consists of 30 members, of whom:

options.A: 15 are from the Lok Sabha and 15 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 20 are from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 10 are from the Lok Sabha and 20 from the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 25 are from the Lok Sabha and 5 from the Rajya Sabha

e: Of the 30 members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, 20 are from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.

q: Part XVII of the Constitution (Official Language) is divided into how many chapters?
e: Part XVII of the Constitution, dealing with Official Language, is divided into four chapters.

q: Under Article 351 of the Constitution, it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of Hindi and to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India, drawing for its vocabulary:

options.D: Primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages

e: Article 351 directs that Hindi shall draw for its vocabulary primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages, while enriching itself by assimilating forms and expressions of other Indian languages.

q: Under Article 343(3) of the Constitution, Parliament may by law provide, for the purposes specified therein, for the use of:

options.C: The numerals of the regional languages

e: Under Article 343(3), Parliament may by law provide for the continued use of the English language, and of the Devanagari form of numerals, for specified official purposes even after the initial fifteen-year period expires.

q: Under Article 348(2) of the Constitution, the use of Hindi or any other language used for official purposes of a State, in the proceedings of a High Court having its principal seat in that State, may be authorised by:

options.A: The Chief Justice of the High Court on his own
options.B: The Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President
options.C: The State Legislature by a simple resolution
options.D: The President, without reference to the State

e: Under Article 348(2), the Governor of a State may, with the previous consent of the President, authorise the use of Hindi or the State's official language in proceedings of the High Court having its principal seat in that State.

q: At present, the number of languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution is:
e: The Eighth Schedule at present includes 22 languages, the number having risen from the original 14 through successive constitutional amendments.

q: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
e: Rajasthani is not included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, whereas Dogri, Bodo and Santhali are among the twenty-two languages included in it.

q: The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on:
e: The Official Languages Act, 1963 came into force on 26 January 1965, when the fifteen-year period contemplated by Article 343 expired.

q: The Official Languages Act, 1963 was amended in 1967 mainly to provide that:

options.A: Hindi would immediately replace English for all official purposes
options.B: The use of English shall continue in addition to Hindi until the Legislatures of the States which have not adopted Hindi as their official language, and both Houses of Parliament, resolve for its discontinuance
options.C: All State Governments would transact their business only in Hindi
options.D: The classification of States into Regions A, B and C would be abolished

e: The 1967 amendment provided that the use of English shall continue in addition to Hindi until the Legislatures of the States which have not adopted Hindi, and both Houses of Parliament, resolve for its discontinuance.

q: Under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of any Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, shall be deemed to be:

options.A: Valid only for guidance of officers
options.B: A summary of the Act for public information
options.C: The authoritative text thereof in Hindi

e: Under Section 5, a Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.

q: Which of the following documents is required to be issued in both Hindi and English under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: A personal letter written by an officer to his family
options.B: The service book of a Government employee
options.C: A confidential note recorded on a file

e: A press communique is one of the documents specified in Section 3(3) and must therefore be issued in both Hindi and English.

q: Under Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court may be authorised by:

options.A: The Governor of the State, with the previous consent of the President
options.B: The Chief Justice of the High Court alone
options.C: The Union Minister of Law and Justice
options.D: The Bar Council of the State

e: Under Section 7, the Governor of a State may, with the previous consent of the President, authorise the use of Hindi or the official language of the State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court.

q: The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India EXCEPT:

options.A: The National Capital Territory of Delhi
options.D: The State of Jammu and Kashmir

e: The Official Language Rules, 1976 apply to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.

q: The classification of States and Union Territories into Region 'A', Region 'B' and Region 'C' for the purposes of the Official Language Policy is laid down in:

options.D: The Annual Programme issued every year

e: The classification of States and Union Territories into Regions A, B and C for the purposes of the Official Language Policy is laid down in the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: Under Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the responsibility for ensuring proper compliance with the provisions of the Official Languages Act and the Rules in a Central Government office rests with:

options.A: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.B: The Section Officer of the establishment branch
options.C: The officer who signs the documents
options.D: The administrative head of the office

e: Under Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the responsibility for ensuring proper compliance with the Act and the Rules rests with the administrative head of the office.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Haryana is placed in:
e: Haryana is a Hindi-speaking State and is placed in Region A under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Gujarat is placed in:
e: Gujarat is placed in Region B under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of West Bengal is placed in:

options.D: It is kept outside all regions

e: West Bengal, a non-Hindi State, is placed in Region C under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the Union Territory of Chandigarh is placed in:
e: The Union Territory of Chandigarh is placed in Region B under the Official Language Rules.

q: Under the Annual Programme for progressive use of Hindi, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'A' is:
e: Under the Annual Programme, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region A is 100 per cent.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature of Central Government offices are required to be printed and published in:

options.B: Diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English

e: Under the Official Language Rules, manuals, codes, forms and other procedural literature are required to be printed and published in diglot form, that is, in Hindi and English.

q: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by:
e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q: The first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti was:
e: Lalit Narayan Mishra was the first Chairman of the Railway Hindi Salahakar Samiti.

q: At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, the work relating to implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the:

options.A: Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari (Chief Official Language Officer)

e: At the headquarters of a Zonal Railway, implementation of the Official Language Policy is looked after by the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari, the Chief Official Language Officer.

q: The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) is mainly responsible for:

options.A: Conducting Hindi examinations for Government employees
options.B: Translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices
options.C: Inspection of offices for use of Hindi
options.D: Organising Hindi Pakhwada in all offices

e: The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) is mainly responsible for translation of codes, manuals, forms and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices into Hindi.

q: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Prabodh course is intended for employees who:

options.A: Have passed the matriculation examination with Hindi
options.B: Have already passed the Pragya examination
options.C: Do not possess any knowledge of Hindi, i.e., beginners
options.D: Are required to do noting and drafting in Hindi

e: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Prabodh course is intended for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi, that is, complete beginners.

q: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, an employee who has passed the Prabodh examination is required to undergo, as the next course:
e: The Hindi Teaching Scheme courses run in the sequence Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, so after passing Prabodh the employee undergoes the Praveen course.

q: In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the course prescribed beyond Pragya, for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work, is:
e: Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work.

q: A Central Government employee shall also be deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi if he:

options.A: Is a native of a Region 'A' State
options.B: Declares himself to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: Has studied Hindi as an optional subject in school
options.D: Has been posted in Region 'A' for one year

e: An employee who declares himself to be in possession of working knowledge of Hindi is also deemed to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.

q: A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing:
e: A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks.

q: A cash award for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing:
e: A cash award for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks.

q: Which of the following incentives is admissible to Central Government employees for passing Hindi, Hindi typing and Hindi stenography examinations under the prescribed schemes?

options.A: Cash award, lumpsum award and personal pay, as admissible under the rules
options.B: Out-of-turn promotion to the next grade
options.C: Additional casual leave of fifteen days every year
options.D: Free railway passes for the whole family

e: For passing Hindi, Hindi typing and Hindi stenography examinations under the prescribed schemes, the admissible incentives are cash award, lumpsum award and personal pay, as per the rules.

q: An employee who passes the Pragya examination with 55% or more but less than 60% marks is entitled to a cash award of:
e: Pragya cash awards are now Rs 6,000 (70% and above), Rs 4,000 (60-70%) and Rs 2,000 (55-60%); no award is admissible below 55% marks. (Source: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, OM No. 21034/25/2024-O.L. (Training) dated 01.07.2025.)

q: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to:

options.A: The best railway station of the year
options.C: The Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy
options.D: The best Division of Region 'A' only

e: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy on Indian Railways.

q: Hindi Pakhwada (Hindi Fortnight) is observed every year in Central Government offices and Railways during:
e: Hindi Pakhwada is observed every year from 14 September to 28 September in Central Government offices and Railways, commencing with Hindi Diwas.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, an employee who possesses working knowledge of Hindi may make noting and drafting on files:

options.D: In Hindi or in English, as he may choose

e: Under the Official Language Rules, an employee possessing working knowledge of Hindi may make noting and drafting on files in Hindi or in English, as he may choose.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication from a Central Government office to a State Government office located in Region 'C' shall be issued in:

options.C: The regional language of the State
options.D: Hindi accompanied by an English translation

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication to a State Government office located in Region C is issued in English.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, if a communication from a Central Government office to an office or person in Region 'A' is issued in English, it must be accompanied by:

options.C: A separate covering letter in Hindi

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a communication issued in English to an office or person in Region A must be accompanied by its Hindi translation.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Central Government office to a State Government office in Region 'B' shall ordinarily be in:

options.B: The regional language of the State
options.D: Either Hindi or the regional language, at the writer's choice

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications to a State Government office in Region B are ordinarily issued in Hindi.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or English.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between Central Government offices situated in Region 'A' (other than those between a Ministry/Department and its attached or subordinate offices) shall be in:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between Central Government offices situated in Region A are required to be in Hindi.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications from a Ministry or Department of the Central Government to its attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A' shall be in Hindi:

options.A: In such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time
options.B: In every case, without any exception
options.C: Only when the subordinate office demands it

e: Communications from a Central Ministry or Department to its attached and subordinate offices in Region A are to be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in:

options.D: The official language of the State only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or English.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in:
e: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, letter-heads used in Central Government offices are required to be printed in Hindi and English.

q: Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, an employee shall be deemed to possess proficiency in Hindi if he has:

options.A: Lived in Region 'A' for ten years
options.B: Worked in the Hindi section of his office for two years
options.C: Been appointed through a Hindi-medium competitive examination
options.D: Passed the Matriculation or an equivalent or higher examination with Hindi as one of the subjects

e: An employee who has passed the Matriculation or an equivalent or higher examination with Hindi as one of the subjects is deemed to possess proficiency in Hindi.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Rajasthan is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Rajasthan, a Hindi-speaking State, is placed in Region A under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Maharashtra is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Maharashtra is placed in Region B under the Official Language Rules.

q: For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, the State of Karnataka is placed in:

options.D: It is not placed in any region

e: Karnataka, a non-Hindi State, is placed in Region C under the Official Language Rules.

q: Under the Annual Programme for the progressive use of Hindi, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region 'B' is:
e: Under the Annual Programme, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in offices located in Region B is 90 per cent.

q: Under the proviso to Article 345 of the Constitution, until the Legislature of a State by law otherwise provides, the language that continues to be used for those official purposes of the State for which it was being used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution is:

options.C: The language of the largest linguistic minority of the State

e: The proviso to Article 345 continues English in use for those official purposes of a State for which it was being used immediately before the commencement of the Constitution, until the State Legislature by law otherwise provides.

q: Under the proviso to Article 346 of the Constitution, if two or more States agree that a particular language shall be the official language for communication between such States, that language is:

options.B: The regional language of either State

e: The proviso to Article 346 provides that if two or more States agree that Hindi shall be the official language for communication between them, Hindi shall be used for such communication.

q: Under Article 120 of the Constitution, a member of Parliament who is unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English may address the House in his mother tongue with the permission of:

options.D: The presiding officer of the House (the Speaker or the Chairman, as the case may be)

e: Under Article 120, a member of Parliament unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English may address the House in his mother tongue with the permission of the presiding officer of the House.

q: Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all Bills introduced in Parliament or in a State Legislature, and of all Acts passed and Ordinances promulgated, shall be in:

options.C: The official language of the State concerned

e: Under Article 348(1), until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all Bills, Acts and Ordinances shall be in the English language.

q: Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, where a State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, that Legislature, a translation of the same in English published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State shall be deemed to be:

options.A: The authoritative text thereof in the English language
options.D: A draft requiring the approval of Parliament

e: Under Article 348(3), an English translation of a State law published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in English.

q: Under Article 344 of the Constitution, after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament on the recommendations of the Official Language Commission, the power to issue directives in accordance with the whole or any part of that report vests in:

options.B: The Union Minister of Home Affairs
options.D: The Chairman of the Official Language Commission

e: Under Article 344, the President may issue directives in accordance with the report of the Official Language Commission after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament thereon.

q: The Presidential Order based on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission, issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament, was issued in the year:
e: The Presidential Order based on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission, issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament, was issued in the year 1960.

q: Section 3(1) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides that, notwithstanding the expiration of the period of fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for:

options.A: The transaction of business in Parliament only
options.B: All the official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament

e: Section 3(1) provides that English may continue to be used, in addition to Hindi, for all the official purposes of the Union and for the transaction of business in Parliament, notwithstanding the expiration of the fifteen-year period.

q: Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with:

options.A: The system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting

e: Under Section 4, the members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, shall be deemed to be:

options.A: A document of no legal value
options.B: Valid only in the States of Region 'A'
options.C: The authoritative text thereof in Hindi
options.D: Effective only after approval by the State Legislature

e: Under Section 6, a Hindi translation of an Act of a State Legislature passed in a language other than Hindi, published in the State's Official Gazette under the authority of the President, is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.

q: Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in:

options.A: The Parliamentary Committee on Official Language
options.C: The Department of Official Language acting alone

e: Under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in the Central Government.

q: The Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003 added which of the following sets of languages to the Eighth Schedule?
e: The Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, raising the number of scheduled languages to 22.
